themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Morris Park
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK, up 1127% from the 8-week baseline average of 1.9 per week, with a z-score of 6.81 indicating an extreme anomaly that suggests either a coordinated tagging campaign or sudden deterioration in city removal response.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1127% spike)
Z-score of 6.81 (severe statistical anomaly; above 2.0 threshold)
Spike emerged in the most recent reporting period with no prior escalation visible in baseline
reporting_angles: Is this a coordinated tagging crew targeting Morris Park, or has city graffiti removal fallen behind?
Interview residents on specific blocks where graffiti appeared; map the geographic concentration

themes_detail.label: Drug activity complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 15 LAST WEEK, up 900% from the 8-week baseline average of 1.5 per week, with a z-score of 6.75, signaling a rapid emergence of visible street-level drug activity or related public safety concerns.
evidence: 15 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD 49th Precinct about enforcement response and whether they've documented a surge
Talk to residents and community board members about which blocks or parks are most affected; check for pattern overlap with panhandling spike

themes_detail.label: Rodent population boom
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints more than tripled to 12 LAST WEEK, up 200% from the 8-week baseline average of 4.0 per week, with a z-score of 5.33, aligning with the community board's repeated pest control budget requests and suggesting a citywide rodent cycle hitting Morris Park hard.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (200% spike)
Community board has listed 'animal and pest control requests including reducing rat and mosquito populations' as a recurring unfunded priority
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to ask if Morris Park is part of a known rodent outbreak zone
Interview residents about visible rat sightings; check if spike correlates with any new construction or waste management changes

themes_detail.label: Overgrown trees and illegal tree damage
themes_detail.summary: Tree-related complaints surged THIS WEEK with overgrown tree/branches at 7 (up 522% from 1.1 weekly baseline) and illegal tree damage at 4 two weeks ago (up 540% from 0.6 weekly baseline), suggesting either storm damage, construction site negligence, or deferred Parks Department maintenance.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (522% spike, z-score 5.04)
Illegal tree damage: 4 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
Combined signal indicates sustained tree management crisis over 2-week window
reporting_angles: Request tree inspection logs from NYC Parks Department to see if Morris Park has a backlog of overgrowth work orders
Cross-reference with DOB permits: are new construction projects (100 new building filings in past 90 days) causing tree damage?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling and street obstruction spike
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped to 9 LAST WEEK (up 620% from 1.2 weekly baseline) and street obstruction spiked to 10 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO (up 264% from 2.8 weekly baseline), indicating emerging quality-of-life issues possibly linked to the drug activity spike and suggesting broader street encroachment problems.
evidence: Panhandling: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (620% spike, z-score 4.96)
Street obstruction: 10 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.8 weekly average (264% spike, z-score 6.05)
Temporal overlap with drug activity spike suggests potential symptom convergence
reporting_angles: Interview business owners and residents on Fordham Road and Morris Park Avenue about visible panhandling encampments
Investigate whether obstruction complaints relate to illegally parked vehicles (2,064 illegal parking complaints in same 90-day window) or homeless encampments
